dataset.title: Results
dataset.description: Two kinds of rows. rowType 'message' is one post: channel, messageId, url, date (the exact UTC timestamp Telegram publishes), text, textLength, views and viewsRaw, viewsApproximate (Telegram's own web preview rounds large counts, so a rounded number is marked instead of being passed off as exact), reactions as a list of {emoji, emojiId, count, approx, paid, kind} where kind is 'emoji' or 'stars' and emoji is null for a custom emoji that has only an id, reactionsTotal, replyToId when the post answers another one, forwardedFrom, authorSignature for signed channels, edited, mediaType (photo, video, album, document, sticker, poll), mediaUrl, mediaTitle, mediaCount, linkPreviewUrl, linkPreviewSite, links, hashtags, mentions, billable. Custom emoji are not media: Telegram paints them as background images, and the actor filters them out instead of claiming media a post does not have. A post cut by the spending cap keeps its identity (channel, messageId, url, date) with text null and a status NOT_CHECKED_CAP plus the reason, so nothing disappears silently. Forward counts and comment counts are NOT in this dataset: Telegram's public web preview does not publish them, and inventing them would be a worse product. rowType 'channel' is one free row per input line: channel title, description, photo, subscribers and subscribersApprox, channelPhotos, channelVideos, channelLinks, messagesSeen (posts the page carried inside the date range, before any limit), messagesDelivered (posts of this channel that reached the dataset), pagesFetched, truncated (true when maxPostsPerChannel cut this channel), status and reason. status READ means posts were delivered; NOT_CHECKED_CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND, NOT_CHECKED_NOT_A_CHANNEL (a group or chat: the web preview covers channels only), NOT_CHECKED_NO_PUBLIC_PREVIEW (the channel exists but shows no public posts), NOT_CHECKED_PRIVATE_INVITE, NOT_CHECKED_INVALID, NOT_CHECKED_DUPLICATE, NOT_CHECKED_LIMIT, NOT_CHECKED_EMPTY (posts exist but none inside sinceDate), NOT_CHECKED_SOURCE, NOT_CHECKED_TIME and NOT_CHECKED_ERROR name the reason in plain words. Only message rows are charged. A message row can also carry NOT_CHECKED_CAP, NOT_CHECKED_ERROR or NOT_CHECKED_CHARGE_UNVERIFIED: the last one means the write raised, the dataset count could not confirm the row either way, and the post is therefore not repeated as a second row.

summary.title: Run summary
summary.description: Run summary kept in the key-value store under RUN_SUMMARY-<runId>, with a plain RUN_SUMMARY copy in the same store (the default store of a run belongs to that run alone, so the copy cannot be overwritten by another run) and that plain key is what the output schema template points at. Channels: channelsRequested, channelsUnique, channelsRead, channelsEmpty (read, but nothing inside the range), channelsUnreadable (not found, a group, no public preview, refused, out of time, error), channelsInvalid (the line is not a channel), channelsCutByLimit, duplicateChannels, and channelsMismatch if unique does not equal read plus empty plus unreadable plus cut. Posts: pagesFetched, messagesSeen, messagesDelivered, messagesCutByLimit, messagesBeforeSinceDate, messagesCap, messagesWriteError (the dataset refused the row), messagesChargeUnverified (the write raised and the count could not settle whether the row landed). rowsDelivered counts every row written, paid ones included. chargedEvents is what the platform actually charged, deliveredUncharged counts message rows that reached the dataset without money. billingActive and billingReason say whether the run could charge at all. stopReason is null, spending-cap, charge-error, dataset-write-error, rate-limited, deadline or empty-input. byStatusChannels and byStatusMessages keep channel and message statuses apart instead of mixing them in one bucket. chargeErrors lists the posts whose write or charge call failed, with the error text. datasetItemCount is our own count of written rows, datasetItemCountApi the same number as the platform reported it, datasetItemCountNote says the platform number was missing or behind. sinceDateParsed, maxPostsPerChannel and maxChannels report the settings actually applied; a sinceDate that cannot be read is refused before any request instead of being ignored. durationSecs and versions (apify, httpx) close the picture. messagesDelivered over messagesSeen is never claimed: a counterMismatch field appears if the numbers ever disagree.
